purpose: Find compatible character graphics, audit the existing private image corpus, and eventually train a tiny anime character generator from random initialization.

policy.notes: Historical baseline was 546 files / 506,492,103 bytes (515 PixAI-prefixed and 31 numeric). Current Git tree snapshot 2026-10-18 has 759 raster images / 706,409,784 bytes (728 PixAI-prefixed names and 31 numeric), adding 213 images beyond that manifest baseline. Original paths/names are kept as provenance clues; base model and LoRA identifiers are explicitly recorded separately and never inferred. Visual content, ownership, terms and training permission remain unreviewed per image.

sources.name: Existing images in this private repository
sources.sourceHint: 728 filenames begin with from-PixAI- and 31 names are numeric in the current tree. Preserve every exact original filename because the user uses names as clues to map images to generation models/LoRAs. Base model/LoRA identifiers must be recorded explicitly; filenames do not establish rights.
sources.useInTraining: only after checking each image's origin, model/source terms, any third-party character rights, and marking training_permission=approved

sources.name: PixAI Terms of Service — generated content
sources.notes: The official terms last updated 2025-07-07 say PixAI does not claim ownership/copyright of AI-generated images and lets the user freely use content they created; users remain responsible for rights and non-infringement. Do not treat this as rights to other users' images, uploaded references, underlying characters, or third-party model files.

sources.name: Kenney Modular Characters
sources.notes: Official/OpenGameArt listing describes 425 separate PNG sprites, 6 spritesheets, and 6 vector files; hundreds of combinations. Generic flat/cartoon style, not the target anime style. Excellent for learning layer alignment and clothing/accessory interchange; inspect archive before integration.

sources.name: PSRC Human Mk2 and Ultimate Devkit
sources.notes: OpenGameArt listing describes torso, limbs, heads, hands, feet, facial features, clothing templates, and a paper-doll rig system. Pixel-art, not anime. Because the linked commercial page has informal license wording, re-check package terms before any redistribution or training use.

sources.name: Anime-style female base sprite
sources.notes: OpenGameArt lists CC-BY 3.0, CC-BY-SA 3.0, and GPL versions on the page and links separate face/hair/armor accessory assets. Do not assume every related file carries the same license; verify the downloaded file and chosen license individually.

sources.name: Modular Character Sprite, Thin Girl — ani mosity
sources.notes: Page says PNGs are separate elements with identical canvases and PSDs; attribution is required. The creator explicitly does not authorize use in generative-AI datasets. Do not use these assets to train this model unless separate explicit permission is obtained.

sources.name: Modular Pixel Character Kit — monapdx
sources.notes: Page advertises aligned transparent PNGs, hairstyles, face/skin variants, GIMP XCF source and a 113 KB ZIP. The page reviewed does not state a standard SPDX/Creative Commons license. Confirm source terms before redistribution or training use.

sources.name: Modular Pixel Character Creator (Female Sprites) — monapdx
sources.notes: This is a separate pack from monapdx-modular-pixel-kit. Page describes consistent body/hair/face/clothing layers in an 86 KB ZIP, but license terms need checking.

sources.name: Anime Girl / Michona — Hordana
sources.notes: OpenGameArt lists CC0 animation strips for jump, walk and blink. Female chibi visual reference, but not separate limbs/clothing components. Verify frame alpha and strip layout before integration.

sources.name: SpriteGAN — small character sprite generator
sources.notes: Paper/repository describes 32x32 RGB sprite GAN trained on 4,272 curated sprites selected from 16,627 CC0 images. Teaches dataset curation and near-duplicate filtering. Do not treat repository code, weights or datasets as incorporated.

sources.name: MDIGAN Characters — paired-view completion
sources.notes: 64x64 RGBA paired-view pose completion task, not free-form character generation. Repository/data rights need review before any reuse.

sources.name: Paper Doll Style Sprites — Andrew Friend
sources.notes: OpenGameArt describes a sizable top-down overlay set with figures, pants, shoes and shirts as separate ZIPs. Requires attribution and ShareAlike for derivatives; generic RPG appearance rather than anime. Inspect the exact selected files and license before reuse or training.

sources.name: Paperdoll Characters (template) — IllusionOfMana
sources.notes: Basic male/female public-domain template. Very small mock-up asset, useful for layout or workflow reference rather than a complete character-part library. Inspect the download before integration.

sources.name: 2D female and male bone-based sprites — buttons
sources.notes: Page describes 2D bone-based sprites designed for rotation/scaling, PNG parts and pivots in filenames. Authors note the figures are lightly dressed/underwear only; additional outfits would need to be created. Useful to test attachment points and articulation, not the final anime style.

sources.name: 80x64 Male and Female Sprites Character Template — mixxit
sources.notes: Page describes an 80x64 template broken into components including clothing and hair, plus walk/shoot/idle animation. Contains male and female examples; the project should select appropriate assets only. Inspect ZIP and pivots before use.

sources.name: Universal LPC Spritesheet Generator
sources.notes: A browser-based sprite compositor with a per-asset licensing/credit approach. Many assets are not anime; useful for studying selection UI and provenance exports. Never treat the whole generator or spritesheets as one blanket license; retain the license/credit info for every chosen part.

sources.name: OverScore Proxy — modular low-poly female character set
sources.notes: OpenGameArt describes a low-poly female base and hundreds of clothing/accessory models under CC0. It is 3D, not a ready-made 2D sprite kit. Consider only for an optional future render-to-sprite pipeline; archive, import format and source page terms still need review.

sources.name: Free CC0 Modular Animated Vector Characters 2D — RGS_Dev
sources.notes: Original itch.io/OpenGameArt listing explicitly states CC0, no credit required, and lists 3 heads, 3 hairs, 7 eyes, 8 mouths, a body, hand, foot, plus idle/walk/roll/jump/hit/death animations on a 2048x2048 canvas. White parts intended for recoloring; visual style is generic cartoon/top-down/side-scroller rather than anime. Use only the original itch/OGA distribution and inspect its package license. A GameDevMarket mirror applies a different Pro License and explicitly says AI training is not allowed there; do not confuse that mirror's terms with the original CC0 source or obtain the training copy from that mirror. Best used first for learning aligned part layering and animation, not as the primary anime-style dataset.
sources.aiTrainingPermission: CC0 on original source page; re-confirm exact downloaded package; style domain mismatch makes it a technical reference by default
sources.redistributionPermission: CC0-1.0 on original itch.io/OpenGameArt listing; retain source link for provenance

sources.name: Anime Character Creator — parametric SVG character generator (rhedak)
sources.license: MIT-code; reference artwork has separate provenance
sources.notes: Repository describes procedural anime-style characters generated from skeleton anchors and independent SVG shapes for heads, faces, hair, arms, legs and layered garments. SVG composition avoids external pretrained weights and is aligned with low-memory rendering. Code is MIT; the README says some character designs began from AI-generated references and several were traced from those references, so do not copy ref/ref-out PNGs/SVGs into our dataset or redistribute them without a separate rights review. Study the skeleton-relative geometry approach; any code adoption must preserve MIT license and be adapted to our restricted female/androgynous target.

sources.name: Anime Girl and Boy Portraits — stevenburrow
sources.notes: OpenGameArt source page confirms CC0 and says the author created the portraits and separated components for recoloring. Archive was downloaded and integrity-tested in the browser research session. XCF contains editable layers; eight RGBA samples are 1000x1000 and SampleAll is 2000x4000. Face/eye/mouth/hair study only; no full body or legs. ZIP not committed to this repository.

packageInspection.dimensions: NewAnime.xcf: 1000x1000; Sample1-Sample8: RGBA 1000x1000 each; SampleAll: RGBA 2000x4000
packageInspection.bundledLicenseOrReadme: No README/LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE/CREDITS text file in ZIP; source page is the CC0 declaration

sources.name: Open Peeps — base asset library
sources.notes: The PeepStudio repository describes Open Peeps art as CC0 and exposes interchangeable hair/body/expression atoms with SVG/PNG export. Generic hand-drawn cartoon, not anime. Use as a reference for modular layers and UI; do not treat the entire community application code as CC0 or as our anime training target.

sources.name: Anime Avatar — konard
sources.notes: Public repository advertises an Unlicense and a configurable anime avatar with modular SVG components for face, eyes, hair, body, legs and background, plus a procedural 3D route. Useful for architecture only; do not copy reference-images, model files or screenshots into the training dataset without separate origin and permission review. WebGL dependency stack is heavier than the first low-memory target.

sources.name: VRoid Studio CC0 sample models (specific alpha releases)
sources.notes: OpenGameArt states these are specific VRoid alpha sample models explicitly released under CC0 and warns some sample models with similar names had more restrictive terms. Verify each model is in the identified CC0 subset before use. They are 3D models, not aligned transparent PNG pieces; consider only for controlled 2D render/reference experiments.

sources.name: Half Body Portrait — Female Cloths
sources.notes: The page lists a single small corset-and-strap PNG that works with a separate half-body portrait template. This is only one clothing example, not a broad wardrobe. Honor the page's Xenodora credit request despite CC0 listing; inspect compatibility before use.

sources.name: Anime Cutout Studio — local character/part extraction application
sources.notes: The repository describes an interactive CPU workflow that exports transparent PNG cutouts, layered PSDs and Spine skeleton trees, including character parts such as hair, head, torso, arms and legs. It requires downloading about 1.7 GB of third-party segmentation/inpainting models; check NOTICE for each model's terms. It does not grant rights to the input illustrations. Use only images the project owns or is authorized to modify; not recommended as the first dependency for the lightweight generator.

sources.name: Face — marionline (editable XCF portrait)
sources.notes: The OpenGameArt page lists a GIMP XCF and several PNG variations with different skin tones, and says no credit is required. This is a face/portrait template rather than a full anime body, modular hair wardrobe or legs. Inspect layer structure and rendering style before selecting any layers.

sources.name: Feminine Humanoid Base Mesh — GoldenThumbs
sources.notes: OpenGameArt lists a small Blender .blend base mesh described as a stylized feminine body with no head. Potentially useful for offline orthographic render experiments or proportions, but it is not an anime PNG kit and provides no head, hair or clothing layers. Verify exact download contents and license metadata before use.

sources.name: Customizable Character Pack — rubberduck
sources.notes: OpenGameArt source page declares CC0 and describes editable GIMP layers for body/skin, shoes, pants, upper clothing and hair, plus 16 sample characters. Archive was downloaded and integrity-tested in the browser research session; XCF and all 16 RGBA PNGs are 64x96. Best first modular assembly experiment at target size, but pixel/cartoon style rather than anime. ZIP not committed to this repository.

packageInspection.bundledLicenseOrReadme: No README/LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE/CREDITS text file in ZIP; source page is the CC0 declaration
